def-finite-product-chaos-input:
## Definition

Fix an integer $d\ge1$, independent real random variables
$Y_1,\ldots,Y_d$ with marginal Borel probability laws $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_d$,
and a degree cutoff vector $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)\in\mathbb N_0^d$. Their joint
law is $\rho=\rho_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\rho_d$, as in
[[thm-independent-random-elements-have-product-joint-law]]. Write
$\Gamma=\prod_{j=1}^d\operatorname{supp}(\rho_j)$, with the product Borel
sigma-algebra. The cutoff vector $p$ is **admissible** when, for every
$j=1,\ldots,d$,
$$\int |y|^{2p_j}\,d\rho_j(y)<\infty$$
and the monomial Gram matrix
$$G_j=(\int y^{r+s}\,d\rho_j(y))_{0\le r,s\le p_j}$$
is positive definite, meaning $c^T G_jc>0$ for each nonzero
$c\in\mathbb R^{p_j+1}$. Throughout the pair, assume the selected cutoff
vector is admissible. The admissible degree box is
$\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^d:0\le\alpha_j\le p_j\text{ for every }j\}$.
Admissibility gives a finite inner product on each stated polynomial space.
It is only a finite-degree condition; it does not assert that polynomials are
dense in any $L^2(\rho_j)$.
def-chaos-total-degree-and-hyperbolic-cr:
## Definition

For $d$ inputs with admissible cutoff vector
$p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)$ from [[def-finite-product-chaos-input]], the cutoff
total-degree set of order $s\ge0$ and cutoff hyperbolic-cross set of
threshold $N\ge1$ are
$$\Lambda^{\mathrm{TD}}_{s,p}=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^d:0\le\alpha_j\le p_j,\ \sum_{j=1}^d\alpha_j\le s\},\qquad
\Lambda^{\mathrm{HC}}_{N,p}=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^d:0\le\alpha_j\le p_j,\ \prod_{j=1}^d(\alpha_j+1)\le N\},$$
The cutoff vector prevents either set from requesting
polynomials above the moment degree declared in
[[def-finite-product-chaos-input]]. Both are finite and contain zero.
An arbitrary finite index set used below is denoted by $\Lambda$; whenever a
downward-closed set is required, this means $\alpha\in\Lambda$ and
$0\le\beta_j\le\alpha_j$ for every $j$ imply $\beta\in\Lambda$.
def-finite-input-bochner-l2-space:
## Definition

Let $(\Gamma,\mathcal B(\Gamma),\rho)$ be the finite product-law probability
space of [[def-finite-product-chaos-input]], and let $V$ be a separable real
Hilbert space. Define $L^2_\rho(V)$ to be the space of strongly measurable
maps $U:\Gamma\to V$ for which
$\int_\Gamma\|U(y)\|_V^2\,d\rho(y)<\infty$, modulo equality
$\rho$-almost everywhere. Its inner product is
$$ (U,W)_{L^2_\rho(V)}=\int_\Gamma (U(y),W(y))_V\,d\rho(y). $$
lem-positive-moment-gram-produces-univar:
## Statement

Let $\rho_j$ be one factor law with admissible degree $p_j$ as in
[[def-finite-product-chaos-input]]. The monomial classes
$1,y,\ldots,y^{p_j}$ are linearly independent in $L^2(\rho_j)$. Applying the
finite Gram–Schmidt recursion to this ordered list gives real orthonormal
polynomials $\phi_{j,0},\ldots,\phi_{j,p_j}$, where $\phi_{j,k}$ has degree
$k$, positive leading coefficient, and $\phi_{j,0}=1$.
def-chaos-orthonormal-tensor-basis:
## Definition

Let $\phi_{j,k}$ be the Gram–Schmidt polynomials from
[[lem-positive-moment-gram-produces-univariate-chaos-polynomials]], and let
$\Lambda$ be a finite subset of the admissible degree box in
[[def-finite-product-chaos-input]]. For $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d)\in\Lambda$,
define
$$\psi_\alpha(y_1,\ldots,y_d)=\prod_{j=1}^d\phi_{j,\alpha_j}(y_j).$$
The **finite polynomial-chaos space** is
$\mathcal P_\Lambda=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_\alpha:\alpha\in\Lambda\}$
inside $L^2(\rho)$. Because $0\in\Lambda$ when a total-degree or
hyperbolic-cross set is used, its constant mode is $\psi_0=1$. No density of
$\mathcal P_\Lambda$ in $L^2(\rho)$ is part of this definition.
def-uniformly-elliptic-affine-random-dif:
## Definition

Let $D\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a bounded polyhedral open set and
$V=H_0^1(D;\mathbb R)$ with norm $\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(D)}$.
[[lem-parabolic-zero-boundary-sobolev-space-is-separable]] supplies the
separable Hilbert structure under Countable Choice; the gradient norm is
equivalent to its Sobolev norm there.

Let $Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_d)$ have the product law $\rho$ of
[[def-finite-product-chaos-input]], and assume its support $\Gamma$ is bounded,
so $|y_j|\le R_j<\infty$ for every $y\in\Gamma$.
For real coefficient functions $a_0,\ldots,a_d\in L^\infty(D)$ define
$$a(x,y)=a_0(x)+\sum_{j=1}^d y_j a_j(x).$$
Assume constants $0<a_*\le a^*<\infty$ satisfy, for every $y\in\Gamma$,
$a_*\le a(x,y)\le a^*$ for almost every $x\in D$. This explicit
all-parameter condition ensures the pointwise variational problem is
well-posed for every stated parameter, not merely almost every one. Let
$F(y)=f_0+\sum_{j=1}^d y_j f_j$ with $f_j\in V^*$.

The pointwise weak form is
$$a_y(u,v)=\int_Da(x,y)\nabla u(x)\cdot\nabla v(x)\,dx=F(y)(v),\qquad v\in V.$$
The Bochner weak form uses the bilinear form
$$\mathcal A(U,W)=\int_\Gamma a_y(U(y),W(y))\,d\rho(y)$$
and the functional $\mathcal F(W)=\int_\Gamma F(y)(W(y))\,d\rho(y)$ on
$L^2_\rho(V)$ from [[def-finite-input-bochner-l2-space]].
lem-chaos-index-sets-are-finite:
## Statement

For every admissible cutoff vector $p\in\mathbb N_0^d$, order $s\ge0$, and
threshold $N\ge1$, the sets $\Lambda^{\mathrm{TD}}_{s,p}$ and
$\Lambda^{\mathrm{HC}}_{N,p}$ of
[[def-chaos-total-degree-and-hyperbolic-cross-index-sets]] are finite and
contain $0$.
thm-finite-input-bochner-l2-is-hilbert:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For the space $L^2_\rho(V)$ of
[[def-finite-input-bochner-l2-space]], the displayed integral pairing is a
well-defined real inner product, its norm is
$$\|U\|_{L^2_\rho(V)}=\left(\int_\Gamma\|U(y)\|_V^2\,d\rho(y)\right)^{1/2},$$
and this norm is complete. Moreover, finite-valued strongly measurable
functions are dense in this space.
alg-christoffel-weighted-least-squares-c:
## Definition

Let $\Lambda$ be finite, contain $0$, and let
$\psi=(\psi_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Lambda}$ be the real orthonormal basis of
[[def-chaos-orthonormal-tensor-basis]]. Set $N=|\Lambda|$ and
$$K_\Lambda(y)=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}|\psi_\alpha(y)|^2.$$
The algorithm takes an evaluable real function $u$, a positive integer sample
count $M$, and independent samples $X_1,\ldots,X_M$ from the probability law
$d\nu=(K_\Lambda/N)\,d\rho$. It forms
$$G=\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M\frac{N}{K_\Lambda(X_i)}\psi(X_i)\psi(X_i)^T,\qquad
b=\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M\frac{N}{K_\Lambda(X_i)}u(X_i)\psi(X_i).$$
If every eigenvalue of $G$ lies in $[1/2,3/2]$, return the unique coefficient
vector $c=G^{-1}b$ and polynomial $\hat u=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}c_\alpha\psi_\alpha$.
Otherwise return `unstable-sample` and no coefficients. The weighted empirical
objective minimized on the accepted branch is
$$\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M\frac{N}{K_\Lambda(X_i)}|u(X_i)-p(X_i)|^2,$$
over $p\in\mathcal P_\Lambda$.
def-finite-chaos-orthogonal-projection:
## Definition

For $u\in L^2(\rho)$ and finite $\Lambda$, define
$$c_\alpha=\langle u,\psi_\alpha\rangle_{L^2(\rho)}=\int u(y)\psi_\alpha(y)\,d\rho(y),\qquad P_\Lambda u=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}c_\alpha\psi_\alpha.$$
The coefficient integral is finite by Cauchy–Schwarz. The finite sum is the
orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal P_\Lambda$ of
[[def-chaos-orthonormal-tensor-basis]].
lem-affine-form-integrable-on-bochner-l2:
## Statement

For the model of [[def-uniformly-elliptic-affine-random-diffusion]], let
$\mathcal H=L^2_\rho(V)$. For $U,W\in\mathcal H$, the scalar functions
$y\mapsto a_y(U(y),W(y))$ and $y\mapsto F(y)(W(y))$ are measurable and
integrable, so $\mathcal A(U,W)$ and $\mathcal F(W)$ are well-defined on
equivalence classes. They satisfy
$$|\mathcal A(U,W)|\le a^*\|U\|_{\mathcal H}\|W\|_{\mathcal H},\qquad
\mathcal A(U,U)\ge a_*\|U\|_{\mathcal H}^2,$$
and
$$|\mathcal F(W)|\le \|F\|_{L^2_\rho(V^*)}\|W\|_{\mathcal H}<\infty.$$
thm-independent-polynomial-chaos-tensors:
## Statement

Let $\rho=\otimes_{j=1}^d\rho_j$ and form $\psi_\alpha$ from
[[def-chaos-orthonormal-tensor-basis]]. Then each $\psi_\alpha$ belongs to
$L^2(\rho)$ and
$$\int_\Gamma\psi_\alpha(y)\psi_\beta(y)\,d\rho(y)=\begin{cases}1,&\alpha=\beta,\\0,&\alpha\ne\beta.\end{cases}$$
In particular, the family indexed by any finite $\Lambda$ is orthonormal and
its constant mode is $\psi_0=1$.
def-chaos-quadrature-coefficient-estimat:
## Definition

Let $\Lambda$ be a finite index set and let $Q$ be any declared finite
cubature functional
$Q(g)=\sum_{q=1}^Jw_qg(y^{(q)})$ whose nodes lie in the domain of evaluation
of $g$. For an evaluable real function $u$, define the quadrature coefficient
and the resulting polynomial by
$$\widehat c_\alpha:=Q(u\psi_\alpha),\qquad
\widehat P_\Lambda u:=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}\widehat c_\alpha\psi_\alpha.$$
The exact coefficients $c_\alpha$ and projection $P_\Lambda u$ are those of
[[def-finite-chaos-orthogonal-projection]]. This definition gives no
accuracy claim for a general cubature rule.
lem-christoffel-sampling-law-and-gram-me:
## Statement

Let $\Lambda$ and $K_\Lambda$ be as in
[[alg-christoffel-weighted-least-squares-collocation]], with
$N=|\Lambda|\ge1$. Then $K_\Lambda\ge1$ pointwise, the measure
$d\nu=(K_\Lambda/N)d\rho$ is a probability measure, and the random matrix
$$A(X)=\frac{N}{K_\Lambda(X)}\psi(X)\psi(X)^T,\qquad X\sim\nu,$$
satisfies $A\succeq0$, $\mathbb E_\nu A=I_N$, and
$\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le N$ almost surely.
thm-affine-random-diffusion-solution-is-:
## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[def-uniformly-elliptic-affine-random-diffusion]],
for each $y\in\Gamma$ there is a unique $u(y)\in V$ satisfying the pointwise
weak problem. The map $y\mapsto u(y)$ is Lipschitz on the bounded parameter
set, strongly measurable, and belongs to $L^2_\rho(V)$. It is also the unique
solution of the Bochner weak equation
$$\mathcal A(u,W)=\mathcal F(W)\qquad(W\in L^2_\rho(V)).$$
thm-finite-chaos-projection-parseval-and:
## Statement

Let $\Lambda$ be finite, contain $0$, and let the real basis
$(\psi_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Lambda}$ be as in
[[def-chaos-orthonormal-tensor-basis]]. For real $u\in L^2(\rho)$ set
$c_\alpha=\langle u,\psi_\alpha\rangle$ and
$P_\Lambda u=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}c_\alpha\psi_\alpha$ as in
[[def-finite-chaos-orthogonal-projection]]. Then
$$\|u\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}c_\alpha^2+
\|u-P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2.$$
The residual is orthogonal to $\mathcal P_\Lambda$,
$\mathbb E[u]=c_0$, and
$$\operatorname{Var}(u)=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda\setminus\{0\}}c_\alpha^2+
\|u-P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2.$$
Here $\operatorname{Var}(u)=\mathbb E[(u-\mathbb E u)^2]$; no completeness of
the polynomial family is assumed.
thm-product-chaos-and-spatial-density-in:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal S$ be the scalar linear span of a declared polynomial-chaos
family in $L^2(\rho)$ and let $V_0$ be a linear subspace dense in the separable
real Hilbert space $V$. Assume separately that $\mathcal S$ is dense in
$L^2(\rho)$; this law-specific completeness hypothesis is not inferred from
finite moments. Then the algebraic tensor span
$$\operatorname{span}\{\,s(\cdot)v:s\in\mathcal S,\ v\in V_0\,\}$$
is dense in $L^2_\rho(V)$.
thm-chaos-quadrature-coefficient-error-s:
## Statement

Let $u\in L^2(\rho)$ be real, let $\Lambda$ be finite, and use the exact and
quadrature coefficients from
[[def-finite-chaos-orthogonal-projection]] and
[[def-chaos-quadrature-coefficient-estimator]]. Then
$$\|u-\widehat P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2
=\|u-P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2+
\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}|\widehat c_\alpha-c_\alpha|^2.$$
Since the finite sum equals
$\|\widehat P_\Lambda u-P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2$, the triangle inequality
also gives
$$\|u-\widehat P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}
\le\|u-P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}
+\|\widehat P_\Lambda u-P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}.$$
Thus coefficient quadrature error and finite-space projection error remain
separate even when no completeness statement is available.
thm-christoffel-gram-concentration-bound:
## Statement

Let $\Lambda$, $N=|\Lambda|\ge1$, and the independent Christoffel samples
$X_1,\ldots,X_M$ be as in
[[alg-christoffel-weighted-least-squares-collocation]]. Let $G$ be its
weighted empirical Gram matrix. For $0<\delta<1$, if
$$M\ge12N\log(2N/\delta),$$
then
$$\mathbb P\{\,\operatorname{spec}(G)\subseteq[1/2,3/2]\,\}\ge1-\delta.$$
thm-stochastic-galerkin-coercivity-and-c:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the affine diffusion hypotheses of
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-affine-random-diffusion]]. Let
$\Lambda\subset\mathbb N_0^d$ be finite and let $V_h\subset V$ be any
finite-dimensional conforming spatial subspace. Define the stochastic
Galerkin space
$$\mathcal V_{\Lambda,h}:=
\operatorname{span}\{\,\psi_\alpha(\cdot)v:
\alpha\in\Lambda,\ v\in V_h\,\}\subset L^2_\rho(V).$$
The Bochner form is continuous with constant $a^*$ and coercive with constant
$a_*$. There is a unique $U_{\Lambda,h}\in\mathcal V_{\Lambda,h}$ satisfying
$$\mathcal A(U_{\Lambda,h},W_h)=\mathcal F(W_h)
\qquad(W_h\in\mathcal V_{\Lambda,h}),$$
and, for the exact solution $u$ of
[[thm-affine-random-diffusion-solution-is-bochner]],
$$\|u-U_{\Lambda,h}\|_{L^2_\rho(V)}
\le\frac{a^*}{a_*}\inf_{W_h\in\mathcal V_{\Lambda,h}}
\|u-W_h\|_{L^2_\rho(V)}.$$
No stochastic-basis completeness or spectral-rate claim is part of this
finite-dimensional estimate.
cor-smolyak-chaos-coefficient-error-boun:
## Statement

Assume $\rho$ is uniform product probability on $[0,1]^d$, so its integral is
$I_d$ in [[thm-smolyak-isotropic-mixed-smoothness-work-error-rate]]. Let
$Q_{\Lambda_n}$ be that theorem's dyadic Simpson Smolyak rule, with
$n\ge2d$. For every $\alpha\in\Lambda$, suppose the coefficient integrand
$g_\alpha=u\psi_\alpha$ has the continuous mixed fourth derivatives and
finite bounds $M_{\alpha,S}$ required by
[[lem-smolyak-mixed-simpson-detail-decay]]. Define
$$E_{\alpha,n}:=C_d\|g_\alpha\|_{\mathrm{mix},d}W_{n,d}^{-4}
(\log(2+W_{n,d}))^{5(d-1)},$$
with the constants and mixed norm of the sparse-grid theorem. Then
$$\left(\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}
|Q_{\Lambda_n}(u\psi_\alpha)-\langle u,\psi_\alpha\rangle|^2\right)^{1/2}
\le\left(\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}E_{\alpha,n}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The error-split theorem consequently bounds the L2 coefficient contribution
by the right-hand side; this claim is restricted to the stated cube law and
mixed regularity.
cor-stochastic-galerkin-fe-interpolation:
## Statement

Assume the hypotheses of the stochastic Galerkin theorem and suppose the
exact solution has the exact finite expansion
$$u(y)=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}u_\alpha\psi_\alpha(y),\qquad
u_\alpha\in H^r(D)\cap H_0^1(D),$$
for an integer $1\le\ell\le r\le k+1$. Let a shape-regular affine mesh have
maximum cell diameter $h$, and assume a globally conforming spatial
interpolant $I_h$ maps these coefficients into its finite-element space,
restricts cellwise to the local interpolants of
[[thm-local-finite-element-interpolation-estimates]], and preserves the
zero boundary condition. Then for the stochastic Galerkin solution
$U_{\Lambda,h}$,
$$\|u-U_{\Lambda,h}\|_{L^2_\rho(H_0^1(D))}
\le \frac{a^*}{a_*}\,C h^{r-1}
\left(\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}|u_\alpha|_{H^r(D)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The regularity and finite-expansion assumptions are explicit; this is not a
general spatial rate for arbitrary random solutions.
thm-weighted-least-squares-stability-and:
## Statement

Let $u\in L^2(\rho)$ be evaluable at the Christoffel samples, and let
$\widehat u$ be the accepted weighted least-squares fit from
[[alg-christoffel-weighted-least-squares-collocation]]. On the event
$\operatorname{spec}(G)\subseteq[1/2,3/2]$, the normal equations have a unique
solution and
$$\|\widehat u-P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}
\le\sqrt2\left(\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M
\frac{N}{K_\Lambda(X_i)}|u(X_i)-P_\Lambda u(X_i)|^2\right)^{1/2},$$
so
$$\|u-\widehat u\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2\le
\|u-P_\Lambda u\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2+
\frac2M\sum_{i=1}^M\frac{N}{K_\Lambda(X_i)}
|u(X_i)-P_\Lambda u(X_i)|^2.$$
For $0<\delta<1$ and $M\ge12N\log(2N/\delta)$, the good event has probability
at least $1-\delta$ by
[[thm-christoffel-gram-concentration-bound]].
cor-tensor-gauss-exact-chaos-coefficient:
## Statement

Suppose each marginal law $\rho_j$ is the positive measure $\mu_j$ in
Gaussian data from [[def-coordinatewise-product-moment-functional]], with
$m_j\ge p_j+1$, where $p$ is the admissible cutoff vector of
[[def-finite-product-chaos-input]]. Let $Q_\otimes$ be the tensor rule of
[[def-tensor-product-gauss-rule]], exact through degree $2m_j-1$ in coordinate
$j$. For every $u\in\mathcal P_\Lambda$ and $\alpha\in\Lambda$, the quadrature
coefficient $Q_\otimes(u\psi_\alpha)$ equals the exact coefficient
$\langle u,\psi_\alpha\rangle$. Hence
$\widehat P_\Lambda u=P_\Lambda u$ and the coefficient quadrature term in
[[thm-chaos-quadrature-coefficient-error-split]] is zero.
